data.narrative:
Atomic Machines is a Series A frontier-semiconductor company founded by Jeff Holden that has raised $144M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 11 private and 3 public peers in Chips & Semiconductors, including private-stage companies such as SambaNova Systems, Cerebras, PsiQuantum, Etched, and Tenstorrent, alongside public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD).

A narrow peer-median approach proved inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage datapoints within the Chips & Semiconductors universe—only one same-stage and one adjacent-stage peer were identified, falling short of the three-point minimum required for reliable cross-sectional analysis. Consequently, the valuation relies on stage-progression methodology. This method applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier, typical for Series A to later-stage advancement, against the $144M total raised as a valuation proxy. This yields an implied valuation of $288M.

The triangulated range, derived from a single applicable method, spans $245M (low) to $331M (high), with a median point of $288M. Given reliance on one methodology rather than multiple triangulation vectors, this analysis carries material uncertainty around stage-progression assumptions and the representativeness of the 2.0x multiplier for this specific subsector. Resolution of valuation uncertainty would benefit from either narrower peer-set construction or direct comparable transaction data within frontier-semiconductor infrastructure.
